artworks.title: Base with Reliefs of the Birth of Zeus
artworks.description: Capitoline base: armed dancers clash shields while the infant Zeus is nursed — the Dictaean Curetes drowning Cronus' hearing. Not Homer's Aetolian Curetes tribe.

artworks.title: Rhea Presents the Swaddled Stone to Cronus (relief)
artworks.description: The trick that sends Zeus to Crete: Rhea's stone for Cronus, then the Curetes' din in the cave — nursery and deceit as one succession myth.

artworks.title: Rhea Handing the Swaddled Stone to Cronus
artworks.description: Attic pelike of Rhea's ruse — the moment before the Curetes take up the hidden child in Crete. Metropolitan Museum of Art.

popCulture.title: Rhea (mythology)
popCulture.description: The mother who hides Zeus with the Curetes and the Dictaean nurses — the Titans' queen as the dancers' employer.

popCulture.title: Zeus
popCulture.description: The infant whose cries the Curetes drown with spear on shield — Crete's hidden king of Olympus.

popCulture.title: Korybantes
popCulture.description: Often conflated with the Curetes in later tradition — armed ecstatic dancers; our Cretan Curetes are Rhea's nursery guard, not the Phrygian Corybantes alone.

popCulture.title: Bibliotheca (birth of Zeus)
popCulture.creator: Apollodorus
popCulture.description: Apollodorus' handbook: Rhea gives Zeus to the Curetes and the nymphs Adrasteia and Ida — the classic nursery roster.
